A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LLaVA-MoD and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite extensive rewriting, relocation, and additional experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original multimodal benchmark results and ablations of distillation, architecture, and teacher capacity in Tables 1–9.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds distillation-strategy, expert/router-capacity, and preference-loss results in Table 7 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The sparse architecture and dense-to-dense/dense-to-sparse pipeline remain unchanged. Preference distillation changes locally: v1 Section 4.1 specifies DPO, whereas v2 Appendix A.1 specifies KTO and Appendix B.2 evaluates both. However, v2 retains the DPO objective in Equation 8, leaving the implemented default insufficiently reconciled.

E1.justification: v1 Section 4.1 explicitly lists AMBER among benchmarks used; v2 removes it. Neither version supplies AMBER results, so this concerns stated evaluation coverage rather than removal of a demonstrated result set. Training dataset sources and all benchmarks with tabulated results are retained.

E2.justification: Table 2 removes IDEFICS-80B, SPHINX-Intern2, LLaVA-Phi, TinyLLaVA, and TinyGPT-V. The remaining main comparators, including those in Table 3, are retained. New ablations introduce a direct-D2S control and an explicit KTO-versus-DPO comparison.

E3.justification: Reported preference-training size changes tenfold, from 0.8M samples in v1 to 80K in v2; the PDFs do not establish whether this corrects documentation or reflects rerunning experiments. New evaluation designs compare combined-data D2S against staged D2D+D2S and vary expert counts and routing capacity. Existing benchmark metrics and splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands design validation: Table 7 tests whether staged mimic distillation is necessary; Appendix B.1 tests four versus eight experts and Top-1 versus Top-2 routing; Appendix B.2 compares KTO and DPO. Earlier preference-stage, token-target, architecture, and teacher-capacity ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2's discussion of training stability introduces no statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: New results include D2S versus D2D+D2S averages of 57.9 versus 60.2 with 1536 versus 960 GPU hours, capacity ablations, and DPO versus KTO Object HalBench response hallucination rates of 20.0 versus 11.4. These are added comparisons, not demonstrated cross-version gains. Table 2 changes Qwen-1.5-based LLaVA-MoD's MME score from 66.7 to 67.6, although Table 4 retains 66.7. Removed comparator rows also remove results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and the shared-vocabulary assumption are retained. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added; KTO is discussed and evaluated without replacing the existing preference-loss formula.

C1.justification: The abstract broadens the preference-distillation contribution from DPO specifically to preference optimization, accompanying the KTO extension. The principal sparse-MoE/progressive-distillation contribution, teacher-surpassing hallucination claim, and headline 8.8% performance and efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that KTO supplies a better preference signal, increasing expert capacity can complicate optimization, and staged distillation balances general and specialized knowledge. Existing comprehension–hallucination tradeoffs and teacher-capacity interpretations remain. The vocabulary-family and memory limitations move to Appendix C without substantive expansion.

D1.justification: v2 removes the promised code-release statement and repository link from the abstract and omits the optimizer epsilon previously specified in Table 11. It adds resource/configuration information for new ablations and names training stages explicitly in the hyperparameter table. Most hardware and training details are relocated rather than newly disclosed.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to KTO and Riquelme et al.'s vision MoE work, while removing numerous background references on data collection/filtering and other models. The overall positioning around combining MoE with knowledge distillation remains. Publication and citation-metadata updates do not constitute new works.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, method explanations, and experimental discussion are extensively condensed and rewritten. Implementation details move into Appendix A, limitations move from Section 6 to Appendix C, and additional experiments form Appendix B. Terminology, subsection presentation, and author/affiliation text also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds five compact experimental tables, including adjacent expert/router tables, and shortens Table 2 through comparator removal. Existing tables receive revised headers, captions, and placement. Figures 1–3 retain their substantive graphics but are resized or repositioned; Figure 3's caption is shortened.

improvement.justification: The new staged-distillation and capacity ablations strengthen validation, and the teacher-capacity discussion is corrected to match its table. However, v2 specifies KTO while retaining the DPO equation, and results previously described under DPO reappear as KTO results without explaining their relationship. The revised MME entry also conflicts with Table 4, and code-access information is removed. These unresolved method/result attribution issues prevent a reliable net quality judgment despite the useful additional evidence.
